name: vercel-react-best-practices
description: Vercel React Best Practices - Performance optimization, RSC boundaries, Server/Client Components, data fetching patterns
author: vercel-labs

rules.title: Prefer React Server Components (RSC)
rules.description: Use Server Components by default in Next.js App Router. Only add 'use client' when interactivity, browser APIs, or client-side state is required.

example.good:
export default async function Page() { const data = await db.query(); return
{data}
; }

rules.title: Eliminate Data Fetching Waterfalls
rules.description: Fetch all required data in parallel at the top level. Do not nest await calls sequentially. Use Promise.all() or TanStack Query for parallel data fetching.

rules.title: Implement Loading UI with streaming
rules.description: Use Next.js loading.tsx files for Suspense boundaries. Show skeletons or placeholders while data streams in.

rules.title: Use Server Actions for mutations
rules.description: Prefer Next.js Server Actions ('use server') over client-side API routes for form submissions and data mutations when possible.

rules.title: Minimize 'use client' boundary
rules.description: Push 'use client' as deep as possible in the component tree. Keep interactive logic isolated to small client components wrapped in server components.

rules.title: Use next/image for all images
rules.description: Never use  tags directly. Use next/image with proper width, height, and priority attributes for LCP optimization.

rules.title: Use next/link for navigation
rules.description: Never use  tags for internal navigation. Use next/link with prefetch for client-side transitions.

rules.title: Use next/font for typography
rules.description: Use next/font/google or next/font/local for self-hosted fonts with automatic subsetting and no layout shift.

rules.title: Use dynamic imports for heavy client libraries
rules.description: Use next/dynamic with ssr:false for client-only libraries (charts, maps, editors) to avoid SSR hydration mismatches.

rules.title: Remove console.log from production code
rules.description: Strip all console.log, console.debug, console.info statements before committing. Use structured logging instead.
